---
title: "Morris-Lecar Model"
subtitle: "Module 1: Low-Dimensional Dynamics"
format: html
---

Morris and Lecar built a model of the voltage oscillations of the barnacle giant muscle fiber, with two non-inactivating conductances: an excitatory calcium current and a potassium recovery current [@morris1981voltage]. Unlike FitzHugh-Nagumo, every term has a physiological meaning.

## The equations

With membrane potential $V$ and the fraction $n$ of open potassium channels,

$$
\begin{aligned}
C\dot V &= I_{\text{app}} - g_{\text{Ca}}\, m_\infty(V)(V - V_{\text{Ca}}) - g_{\text{K}}\, n\,(V - V_{\text{K}}) - g_L (V - V_L),\\
\dot n &= \phi\,\frac{n_\infty(V) - n}{\tau_n(V)},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ml}

$$
m_\infty(V) = \tfrac12\left[1 + \tanh\frac{V - V_1}{V_2}\right],\quad
n_\infty(V) = \tfrac12\left[1 + \tanh\frac{V - V_3}{V_4}\right],\quad
\tau_n(V) = \operatorname{sech}\frac{V - V_3}{2V_4}.
$$

The calcium activation $m$ is assumed instantaneous, $m = m_\infty(V)$, which reduces the model to two variables [@morris1981voltage]. This is the form given by Lecar in [Scholarpedia](http://www.scholarpedia.org/article/Morris-Lecar_model), with the rate constant written as $\phi$.

`amlab/odes_2d/morris_lecar.py` implements @eq-ml with default values $C = 20$, $g_{\text{Ca}} = 4$, $g_{\text{K}} = 8$, $g_L = 2$ (conductances in mS/cm², capacitance in µF/cm²), $V_{\text{Ca}} = 120$, $V_{\text{K}} = -84$, $V_L = -60$, $V_1 = -1.2$, $V_2 = 18$, $V_3 = 2$, $V_4 = 30$ (all in mV) and $\phi = 0.04$. The results below are for these values.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-ml
#| fig-cap: "Morris-Lecar model with the amlab default parameters. Left: V(t) for three applied currents, starting at V = -60 mV, n = 0. Right: phase plane for I_app = 150 with the V-nullcline (blue), the n-nullcline (red) and the limit cycle."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.8
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

from amlab.odes_2d.morris_lecar import morris_lecar

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.8))
for i_app in [60.0, 150.0, 260.0]:
    sol = solve_ivp(morris_lecar, (0, 500), [-60.0, 0.0], args=(i_app,), method="LSODA",
                    max_step=1.0, rtol=1e-8)
    ax1.plot(sol.t, sol.y[0], lw=1, label=f"I_app = {i_app:.0f}")
ax1.set_xlabel("t (ms)")
ax1.set_ylabel("V (mV)")
ax1.legend(fontsize=8)

v = np.linspace(-70, 50, 400)
i_app, g_ca, g_k, g_l, v_ca, v_k, v_l = 150.0, 4.0, 8.0, 2.0, 120.0, -84.0, -60.0
m_inf = 0.5 * (1 + np.tanh((v + 1.2) / 18))
n_inf = 0.5 * (1 + np.tanh((v - 2) / 30))
ax2.plot(v, (i_app - g_ca * m_inf * (v - v_ca) - g_l * (v - v_l)) / (g_k * (v - v_k)), "b", lw=1)
ax2.plot(v, n_inf, "r", lw=1)
sol = solve_ivp(morris_lecar, (0, 500), [-60.0, 0.0], args=(i_app,), method="LSODA",
                max_step=1.0, rtol=1e-8)
ax2.plot(sol.y[0][sol.t > 200], sol.y[1][sol.t > 200], "k", lw=1.2)
ax2.set_ylim(-0.05, 0.8)
ax2.set_xlabel("V (mV)")
ax2.set_ylabel("n")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## What the simulations show

With these parameters:

- for small currents ($I_{\text{app}} = 60$) the model rests at a stable fixed point;
- for intermediate currents ($I_{\text{app}} = 150$) it fires periodically;
- for large currents ($I_{\text{app}} = 260$) the membrane stays depolarized at a new stable fixed point.

The rest state loses stability through a pair of complex eigenvalues, a Hopf bifurcation. You can locate it with the numerical Jacobian of [CDIMA: Stability and the Hopf Point](cdima-stability.qmd):

```{python}
from scipy.optimize import brentq, fsolve


def max_real_eigenvalue(i_app, h=1e-6):
    fp = fsolve(lambda y: morris_lecar(0, y, i_app), [-30.0, 0.1])
    jac = np.zeros((2, 2))
    for j in range(2):
        e = np.zeros(2)
        e[j] = h
        jac[:, j] = (morris_lecar(0, fp + e, i_app) - morris_lecar(0, fp - e, i_app)) / (2 * h)
    return np.linalg.eigvals(jac).real.max()


print(f"Lower Hopf point: I_app = {brentq(max_real_eigenvalue, 90, 110):.1f}")
print(f"Upper Hopf point: I_app = {brentq(max_real_eigenvalue, 220, 240):.1f}")
```

Simulations started far from rest already oscillate for $I_{\text{app}} \approx 96$, below the lower Hopf point near 101.8. In that range a stable rest state and a stable limit cycle coexist, which indicates a subcritical Hopf bifurcation for this parameter set. Other parameter sets make the Morris-Lecar model start firing through a saddle-node bifurcation instead, at arbitrarily low frequency; this is why it is used to compare different classes of neural excitability [@ellner2006dynamic].

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise
Derive the $V$-nullcline shown in @fig-ml from @eq-ml.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
Set $\dot V = 0$ and solve for $n$:
$n = \dfrac{I_{\text{app}} - g_{\text{Ca}} m_\infty(V)(V - V_{\text{Ca}}) - g_L(V - V_L)}{g_{\text{K}}(V - V_{\text{K}})}$. The $n$-nullcline is $n = n_\infty(V)$.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
